column1: # MediaDB family (naming) vocabulary  -- versioned input, NOT generated at run time
# THIS IS THE NAMING REGISTRY. It is deliberately SEPARATE from the COMPOSITION
# registry in tools/base_media.py (BASES) and from the canonical formulations in
# tools/curate_wellknown_media.py (REGISTRY). Assigning a family here must NEVER
# cause any component to be injected into a medium. Composition rewriting and
# family labelling are different operations; conflating them is what let a
# hamburger inherit LB's yeast-extract decomposition (finding NM-01).
# Seeded from tools/curate_wellknown_media.py REGISTRY (262 entries, each with its
# own formulation citation) plus the families named in the 2026-09 audit that the
# registry lacked (ISP-1..5, CGXII, YCFA, marine 2216, RPMI, DMEM, Widdel, Davis,
#   family_id       stable snake_case key. Never rendered; used for grouping.
#   display_label   human label shown in the browser.
#   name_regex      matched against the CLEANED MEDIUM NAME ONLY. Never against
#                   `description` - 701 food descriptions say "plus a standard M9
#                   mineral base" and 0 food names say M9 (NM-01 verification (6)).
#   alias_of        this family is the SAME medium as the named family; collapse into it.
#   parent_family   this family is a REFINEMENT of the named family (LBv2 of LB,
#                   BG-11_0 of BG-11); the child wins and the parent is recorded.
#   reference_id    id of the canonical std_* record whose composition is used to
#                   corroborate a name match. Empty = no reference available, so
#                   the family stays method='name_only' and is never promoted.
# A family match is a HYPOTHESIS. normalize_names.py promotes it to
# 'name_and_composition' only if the record's non-injected exchange set overlaps
# the reference composition; otherwise it stays 'name_only' and says so.
